purpose: Prepare the deterministic turn/combat state machine increment for Emberfall v0.2. This is a Grounding packet only; implementation is not authorized until EFB-002 has passed independent Mastery, EFB-000 merged-tree review is accepted, and EFB-002 Repetition is recorded.

constraints: No implementation until EFB-002 independent Mastery PASS/accepted disposition, EFB-000 merged-tree review, EFB-002 Repetition, a real independent-review dispatch route and durable Maestro state continuity are complete.
Preserve all accepted v0.2 rules and Product Owner decisions. Do not re-litigate closed ADRs.
Pure Kotlin/JVM simulation remains independent of Android APIs; no Android UI in this increment.
Use a deterministic command/reducer architecture. UI preview must be pure and must not consume RNG or mutate state.
The phase order is Draw -> Weave -> Cast -> Wall -> Enemy -> Cleanup.
Starting player resources and turn rules come from v0.2 spec: 70 Vigil, 2 Flasks (max 5, heal 30), 3 base Taps, Block absorbs damage and resets each turn, 5-card draw.
Enemies show two upcoming intents with numeric effects/targets; resolved intent must equal the forecasted intent.
Board action results are consumed from EFB-002. Do not duplicate or fork board mechanics.
No card definitions/effect DSL beyond the combat integration boundary; those belong to EFB-004.
No class-specific content, run progression, Android UI, art, audio or backend in EFB-003.
Invalid actions are transactional: no partial state, resource or RNG mutation.
Every transition emits deterministic events; event ordering is explicit and replayable.
No unapproved merge, publish, store submission or deploy; no secrets in commits or logs.

risks: R1: incorrect phase order can create double Wall rises, missed intents or unintended card/board timing.
R1: intent preview and resolution can diverge if RNG or state mutation occurs during preview.
R1: Block reset timing, damage ordering, Delay and status durations can create hidden or exploitable outcomes.
R1: enemy board attacks may target sealed, missing or invalid cells unless target legality is explicit.
R1: lethal damage, Flask use and end-turn cleanup can leave partially committed states without atomic transitions.
R1: premature card integration will entangle EFB-003 and EFB-004; define interfaces only.
P1: legacy prototype license/ownership/reuse rights are not evidenced; EFB-003 must not copy legacy source or assets.
P1: EFB-002 remains an unaccepted draft candidate; do not code against its API as a frozen contract until Mastery/Repetition acceptance.
acceptance: Explicit state machine covers Draw, Weave, Cast, Wall, Enemy and Cleanup with legal transitions and phase-specific commands.
Player state models Vigil, Block, Flask count/cap and death; resource bounds are enforced.
Block absorbs damage and resets at the specified turn boundary; exact damage order has golden tests.
Weave enforces the available Tap count and consumes a Tap only on a successful legal board action; rejected actions do not mutate state.
Enemy intent model exposes the next two intents, including numeric effect and target.
The intent shown to the player is exactly the intent resolved; preview is pure and deterministic.
Implement spec-defined intents: Strike, Ash Row, Stone Seed, Stain, Fog, Seal, Brand, Surge, Snatch and Curse, within EFB-003 scope and without card-specific effects.
Delay/status duration and target resolution are deterministic and have explicit ordering.
Wall phase uses the EFB-002 board API and preserves its accepted Overflow/Seal contracts.
Death, Flask healing, max-Flask handling and cleanup edge cases are covered.
All invalid commands reject atomically and leave state/RNG unchanged.
Command replay with seed + rules version + action log yields identical checkpoint hashes.
Golden tests cover every phase transition and every enemy intent; property/fuzz tests cover legal command sequences across many seeds.
Pure-JVM Gradle/JUnit, formatting/lint, deterministic replay and Maestro GateRunner checks pass on the exact candidate SHA.
Independent Mastery review inspects exact candidate, changed paths, tests and evidence; builder and reviewer identities differ.
Repetition records expected/actual outcome, durable lessons, accepted state and next increment.
next_increment: After EFB-002 acceptance and Repetition, start the EFB-003 Maestro workflow, ground the exact turn/combat interfaces, then implement one bounded player-vs-first-enemy vertical combat slice before broadening enemy content.
